Hypothesis_Test_1.Name: Two-Sample Welch's T-Test: Insured vs Uninsured Patient Billing Amounts
Hypothesis_Test_1.Business_Question: Do insured patients incur different healthcare billing amounts compared to uninsured patients?
Hypothesis_Test_1.H0: Mean billing amount for insured patients is equal to uninsured patients (mu_insured = mu_uninsured)
Hypothesis_Test_1.H1: Mean billing amount for insured patients differs significantly from uninsured patients (mu_insured != mu_uninsured)
Hypothesis_Test_1.Interpretation: Fail to reject H0: No statistically significant difference in billing amounts between insured and uninsured cohorts at alpha = 0.05.

Hypothesis_Test_2.Name: One-Way ANOVA: Patient Satisfaction Across 20 Health Facilities
Hypothesis_Test_2.Business_Question: Does patient satisfaction rating differ significantly across the 20 healthcare facilities in Rwanda?
Hypothesis_Test_2.H0: Mean patient satisfaction is identical across all 20 healthcare facilities (mu_1 = mu_2 = ... = mu_20)
Hypothesis_Test_2.H1: At least one healthcare facility has a statistically significantly different mean patient satisfaction rating
Hypothesis_Test_2.Interpretation: Fail to reject H0: Patient satisfaction ratings are statistically homogeneous across all 20 facilities (p >= 0.05).

Hypothesis_Test_3.Name: Chi-Square Test of Independence: Hospital Admission Rates Across Patient Age Groups
Hypothesis_Test_3.Business_Question: Is the likelihood of requiring hospital admission significantly dependent on patient age group?
Hypothesis_Test_3.H0: Hospital admission is independent of patient age group (P(Admitted | Age Group) = P(Admitted))
Hypothesis_Test_3.H1: Hospital admission is significantly dependent on patient age group
Hypothesis_Test_3.Interpretation: Fail to reject H0: Admission rates do not exhibit statistically significant dependency on age group.
